lesson_title: Circles, Fences and Two Downhill Slopes: Geometry, Statistics and Finance Essentials
hook_text: Same bakkie. Same 20% loss per year. One formula leaves you R13 440 richer.
clip_script: Straight-line depreciation is simple interest in reverse: A equals P, times, one minus i n. A bakkie of one hundred and twenty thousand rand losing twenty percent per year for three years: one hundred and twenty thousand times, one minus nought comma six — forty-eight thousand rand. Reducing-balance depreciation is compound in reverse: A equals P, times, one minus i, to the power n. Same bakkie, same rate: one hundred and twenty thousand times nought comma eight cubed — sixty-one thousand four hundred and forty rand. Reducing balance keeps more value, because each year's twenty percent bites a smaller amount. Same rate, thirteen thousand four hundred and forty rand apart — the formula choice IS the question.
visual_style: Two identical bakkies roll down two slopes side by side — one a straight ramp losing equal chunks, one a bouncing curve losing shrinking chunks; rand counters tick down at different speeds until the gap flashes between them at the bottom.
mood: Split-screen suspense — identical setup, diverging fortunes, one word in the question deciding everything.
pacing: Parallel build on the two slopes, tick-tock of the counters, sharp reveal of the gap, crisp takeaway.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and let the wording pick the formula before the marker picks your marks.
